entries.reason: the release carries no command event class at all: read with tools/mach32_methods.py from the 6.1.3 armv7 cache, none of its 236 classes in the MediaPlayer image at 0x31fe3000 has a name holding CommandEvent and none of its 41 categories adds one, with a nonsense selector absent as the control; and all 236 were read and none declares this member's selector. That is a per-class answer, which is what decides a member: the release's whole-cache selector list (selectors_armv7.txt, 113981 distinct names) has a line for repeatType, shuffleType and isNegative because other frameworks declare those names, which is the trap facts/MediaPlayer/MPMediaItem.md:105 records for albumTrackNumber. A class the release does not have is new code and cannot shadow anything, so there is nothing native for it to be. This class is the public ancestor of four events the port already carries, so the chain a caller walks was missing a link Apple's own chain has. THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS ROW CLAIMED THE PORT'S FOUR CARRIED EVENTS WALK A CHAIN THROUGH THIS CLASS, and the header says otherwise: MPRemoteCommandEvent.h at 26.2 declares MPRatingCommandEvent, MPSkipIntervalCommandEvent, MPChangePlaybackRateCommandEvent and MPChangeLanguageOptionCommandEvent all as ': MPRemoteCommandEvent', and grep for '@interface.*: MPFeedbackCommandEvent' over MediaPlayer.framework/Headers finds nothing in 26.2 and nothing in 16.4 - no class Apple publishes derives from it. The row stands on the class being public API at MP_API(ios(7.1)) that the release carries neither of, and nothing more. APPLE PUBLISHES NO API THAT HANDS A COMMAND AN EVENT, so there is no delivery path to wire - on this release or any other. grep -rn 'deliverEvent|sendEvent' over MediaPlayer.framework/Headers reads NO file in SDK 26.2 and no file in 16.4, and MPRemoteCommand's public surface is exactly enabled, addTarget:action:, removeTarget:action:, removeTarget: and addTargetWithHandler:. An application sets a handler; only the system invokes it. 'deliverEvent:' is a PRIVATE selector on MPRemoteCommandCenter that no header declares, which is why the 6.1.3 selector universe's 113981 distinct names cannot hold it either - the 236 classes have no MPRemoteCommand to declare it - and why no file under packages/a/apple-backports/ defines it either, the name appearing only in this family's own prose about it. The port's own -charon_dispatch: (MPRemoteCommandCenter71.m:133) is reached from exactly one place, the subtype switch at :250-275, which maps ten UIEventSubtypeRemoteControl* cases; UIEvent.h in SDK 26.2 AND 16.4 declares exactly those ten, 100 through 109, with no feedback case at any availability, so no UIEvent on any iOS can carry one. MPFeedbackCommand's own row in ios71remotecommand.json has said 'never messaged by this port's own bridge, since no old-style feedback gesture exists' since it landed; this row now says the same about the event it belongs to THE LINE THAT PRODUCED THE FALSE CLAIM IS MPRemoteCommandCenter71.m:33, which says charon_command() "creates them lazily by class regardless of which object file defines them". That sentence is TRUE and it is about the COMMAND objects - MPRemoteCommand and its subclasses, which is what charon_command() allocates. Reading it as covering the events is what this row did; the next reader should not.
entries.effect: NSClassFromString answers the class and a caller-constructed event is an instance of it, so [MPFeedbackCommandEvent new] allocates a real object instead of messaging nil. It is never messaged by the port's own bridge, for the reason the row says
